title: An invertible sheaf of nonpositive degree on every component of a connected reduced curve has no nonzero sections unless it is trivial
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for an invertible sheaf L on a proper, reduced, connected, equidimensional scheme of dimension one whose restriction to every irreducible component has nonpositive degree, either H^0(X, L) vanishes or L is trivial. The proof takes a nonzero section s, uses reducedness to find a component C on which s restricts nontrivially, and invokes the degree criterion on curves to conclude that s is nowhere vanishing on C (proof lines 9986-9990). It then propagates nowhere-vanishing to every component meeting C and uses connectedness to conclude that s vanishes nowhere, whence L is trivial (proof lines 9991-9994). H2: the propagation of nowhere-vanishing across the components using connectedness is the substance.
